title: Whitelist the Sort
prompt: Implement sorted_users(conn, sort) where sort is 'name' or 'id' — the ONLY two allowed columns. Map through a whitelist and raise ValueError for anything else. Return list of (id, name).

tests.name: valid sorts work
tests.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.execute('CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)')
conn.executemany('INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)', [('B',), ('A',)])
assert sorted_users(conn, 'name') == [(2, 'A'), (1, 'B')]
assert sorted_users(conn, 'id') == [(1, 'B'), (2, 'A')]
tests.hint: ORDER BY the whitelisted column name.

tests.name: unknown sort rejected
tests.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.execute('CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)')
try:
    sorted_users(conn, 'name; DROP TABLE users')
    failed = False
except ValueError:
    failed = True
assert failed
tests.hint: Anything outside {'name', 'id'} raises ValueError before touching SQL.
